lessons.correction: Increase your air presence to counter potential drops or air threats, continue strengthening your ground army, and maintain your economy.

lessons.title: Midgame Ground vs. Air Flexibility
lessons.when: At around 540 seconds, both players have transitioned to a midgame ground army with Siege Tanks, Marines, and supporting units. The opponent shows moderate air presence.
lessons.why: With both players having similar ground compositions, adding air units provides flexibility and counters potential medivac drops or air harassment.

lessons.correction: Continue strengthening your ground army, increase your air presence, and maintain your economy to support a long fight.
lessons.mistake: Tempting to overcommit to ground forces and neglect air upgrades or economy, potentially losing a prolonged engagement due to lack of air support or resource exhaustion.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you have more information about the opponent's tech or when you are ready to take a decisive fight.
lessons.title: Late Midgame Sustained Pressure
lessons.when: At around 600 seconds, both players have a heavy ground army with Siege Tanks and Marines, and a moderate air presence. The opponent has a heavy defense.
lessons.why: With both players having strong ground armies, adding air units and maintaining a robust economy gives you an edge in the late game.

lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you have more information about the opponent's composition or when you reach a new tech milestone.
lessons.title: Early Midgame Economy and Defense
lessons.when: At around 300 seconds, both players have a heavy economy and technology investment, with a ground-oriented army. The opponent shows possible pressure with Reapers and Hellions.
lessons.why: Both players are in a similar economic and technological state. Maintaining a strong economy and technology lead while building a versatile ground army positions you well for the midgame.
